entries.claim: Task 2 commits a tracked .mjs file that the existing `**/*.mjs` ignores in eslint.config.js:159 and .jscpd.json:4 then skip, which can count as widening a skip-list exemption. The plan's own Notes (line 100) say so, but they leave the ruling to the owner after the commit instead of making Task 2 wait for it.
entries.failure_scenario: Task 2 lands `.github/cadence/coverage-report-check.mjs` with the gitignore negation. From then on eslint and jscpd skip a tracked source file. The plan admits the template fails `no-undef` 4 times when linted. hqptuner2/CLAUDE.md says widening an exemption is a new exemption, approved before it is written, and AC5 says no exemption is added. So if the owner rules it a widening, the phase has already committed it without approval and broken AC5. The plan needs an owner ruling (or a node-globals lint block) before Task 2's commit, not after.

entries.claim: The plan discloses footprint only for Task 6's suite run. The pre-commit `pytest-offline` hook is `always_run: true` (.pre-commit-config.yaml:91-101), so every commit in Tasks 1-5 also runs the full offline suite, and none of those runs is disclosed.
entries.failure_scenario: Each per-task commit (five or more) runs `make pytest-offline`: 3673 tests, about 39 s on one full core. ~/dev/CLAUDE.md 3.1 requires naming any action that reaches a full core for 10 s before it runs, and the plan names only Task 6's run.

entries.claim: Read literally, Task 4's last verify check can never pass. It says every `run:` value of the check job contains exactly one pytest invocation and exactly one `--experimental-test-coverage`.
entries.failure_scenario: The `install` step's run value and the `make lint lint-js` step contain no pytest, so a check written to the letter fails. The step `make -o pytest-offline test` and the `scripts/pytest_plugins` PYTHONPATH also contain the substring `pytest`, so a substring count overcounts. The verify works only if it is read as one invocation across all the job's run values, and the plan never states that.
